name: Tura Peak
description: Majestic peak on the eastern flank of Tura town offering panoramic views of the Brahmaputra plains and Bangladesh on clear days. Moderate trek through reserve forest with British-era path, Cinchona plantation, and wildlife like hornbills and gibbons.
facts: Local legend links name to Dura/Durama.
5-7 km from Tura town with footpath from British times.

name: Nokrek National Park / Biosphere Reserve
description: UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and National Park in the Nokrek range, highest peak in Garo Hills. Home to rare Citrus indica (Memang Narang), hoolock gibbons, elephants, red pandas, and rich biodiversity. Trekking and nature trails available.
facts: Established as National Park in 1986, UNESCO Biosphere 2009.
Core area about 47.48 km² spanning West, East, North Garo Hills.
Source of major rivers like Simsang.

name: Pelga Falls
description: Scenic waterfall 7 km from Tura on the Ganol River, popular for picnics, angling, and short walks. Features a traditional Garo bamboo bridge and viewpoints developed for tourism.
facts: Traditional bamboo bridge over Ganol River.

name: Rongbang Dare Waterfall
description: Multi-tiered waterfall near Chinabat/Rombagre village on the Tura-Williamnagar road, tributary of Simsang River. Surrounded by bamboo forests, with hanging bridge for views; best during monsoon.
facts: About 37 km from Tura on Tura-Williamnagar Road.
Visible from the highway with short descent to base.

name: Aminda Rangsa Art Village
description: Offbeat cultural village known for wood and stone carvings by local artisans like Handum Marak, celebrating Garo motifs. Clean village with sustainable art focus, about 20-27 km from Tura.
facts: Famous for intricate Garo cultural sculptures.

name: Wadagokgre Archaeological Site
description: Ancient fortified archaeological site near Bhaitbari/Phulbari with remnants of a 4th-century AD city, stupas, and temples once on the Brahmaputra bank. Protected ASI-related site with Buddhist and Hindu elements; currently under conservation.
facts: 15 km stretch of protected ancient fortified area.
Near Bhaitbari, about 60 km from Tura; access restricted in parts.

name: Rombagre Fish Sanctuary
description: Community-managed fish sanctuary on the Simsang River at Rombagre village, protecting chocolate mahseer and other species. Clear waters allow viewing schools of fish; model for community conservation.
facts: About 35-37 km from Tura on Tura-Williamnagar road.

name: Chandigre Village
description: Rural tourism village near Nokrek with traditional bamboo houses, orchards, forest trails, and resort. Offers cultural immersion in Garo lifestyle amid hills.
facts: About 30-34 km from Tura, near Nokrek.

name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and East Khasi Hills HQ, known as the Scotland of the East. Pine-clad hills, colonial architecture, markets, lakes, and gateway to Khasi attractions.

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at ~1966 m, sacred to Khasis as home of deity Lai Shyllong. Panoramic views of city, hills, and Bangladesh plains; IAF radar station nearby.
facts: Best clear days for Himalayan views.

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall (Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew) on the outskirts of Shillong. Named after a rock resembling an elephant destroyed in 1897 quake; lush ferns and easy access.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: One of the wettest places on Earth, gateway to waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges. Dramatic limestone cliffs, heavy rainfall, and Khasi culture.

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: India's tallest plunge waterfall (~340 m) plunging into a turquoise pool near Sohra. Fed by plateau rains; linked to local legend of Ka Likai.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge grown from Ficus elastica by Khasi people over generations in Nongriat village. Requires ~3500-step trek from Tyrna; UNESCO tentative list.
facts: Part of Jingkieng Jri cultural landscape.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Renowned as Asia's cleanest village with 100% literacy, bamboo dustbins, and living root bridge nearby at Riwai. Matrilineal Khasi community near Bangladesh border.

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint meaning 'end of the hills', offering panoramic 360° views of green valleys and ridges ~25 km from Shillong. Popular for sunrise and photography.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient protected sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) of ~78-192 acres near Mawphlang, preserved by Khasi beliefs for centuries. Rich biodiversity, monoliths, no extraction of anything allowed.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra with stalactites, stalagmites, and narrow passages. Formed by water erosion; electric lighting for ~150 m tourist section.

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters)
description: Seven-segmented waterfall ~315 m high plunging over limestone cliffs south of Mawsmai. Dramatic during monsoon; views of Bangladesh plains.
facts: Also called Mawsmai Falls or Seven Sisters.

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning multi-tiered waterfall near Amlarem with vivid turquoise pools, limestone cliffs, and dense forest surroundings. Popular for swimming (with life jackets), photography, and short treks; one of Meghalaya's most photogenic falls.
facts: About 30 km from Jowai and 90 km from Shillong.
Entry fee around ₹50; life jackets available.
Best in post-monsoon to winter for clear water.

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest concentration of megalithic monoliths in Meghalaya, with menhirs and dolmens erected between 1500–1835 AD by Jaintia clans and kings. Includes the tallest menhir (~8 m) linked to legend of Mar Phalyngki.

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: Historic ~600-year-old Hindu temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, where Goddess Durga is worshipped as Jayanti. Unique blend of tribal and Hindu traditions; major pilgrimage site especially during Durga Puja.
facts: One of 51 Shakti Peethas; left thigh of Sati associated.
About 25 km from Jowai, near the monoliths.
Priests are descendants from original Jaintiapur lineage.

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake (also Pung Sajar Nangli) beside NH-6 near Mukhla, created according to legend by rebel general Sajar Nangli and followers. Popular picnic and boating spot with pine-lined shores.
facts: About 10 km from Jowai on Shillong-Jowai highway.
Legend of digging with bows by 290 clans.
Scenic views and calm waters ideal for relaxation.

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Crystal-clear Umngot (Dawki) River at the India-Bangladesh border town of Dawki, famous for transparent waters revealing the riverbed and historic 1932 suspension bridge. Boating and border views popular.
facts: Best clarity in dry winter months (Nov–Mar).

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village upstream from Dawki on the Umngot River, known for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, and clearer quieter waters. Emerging eco-tourism and adventure base away from main border crowds.
facts: Popular for riverbed camping in season.

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Cascading multi-tier waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road, accessible via a short walk over an arch bridge through paddy fields. Lesser-known alternative to more crowded falls.
facts: Short walk from highway via arch bridge.

name: Jowai
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district and cultural hub of the Pnar people. Plateau town surrounded by Myntdu River, gateway to waterfalls, lakes, monoliths, and border attractions.

name: Ialong Park
description: Eco-park about 8 km from Jowai featuring sacred groves and panoramic viewpoints over the Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River. Developed for nature walks, picnics, and eco-tourism.
facts: About 8 km from Jowai on Jowai-Silchar road.
Views of paddy valleys and river.

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered waterfall near Shkentalang/Jarain village with turquoise pools and forested canyon setting. Requires a short hike; emerging hidden gem for offbeat nature lovers.
facts: Short 15–20 minute hike from parking near Shkentalang.
Also known locally in connection with 'paradise' falls.
